overview.title: Child development, communication and participation
overview.lead: Ages 0–18, with two clearly separated adult learning paths: caregiver education and professional preparation.

sections.title: Why this field matters
sections.text: Communication, movement, emotional well-being and everyday access affect how children participate in family, school and community life. Support should begin with the child’s priorities, strengths, relationships and rights. A diagnosis is not a complete portrait of a person.

sections.title: Two paths with shared foundations
sections.text:
The 12 shared topics cover development from infancy through adolescence, observation/referral, assent and privacy, communication, movement/sensory participation, emotional context, inclusion and health boundaries.

The caregiver path adds 12 workshops on responsive interaction, speech/fluency support, AAC, multilingual homes, routines, sensory access, co-regulation, school, adolescence, mental health, teamwork and a fictional portfolio. The professional path adds 16 topics on scientific prerequisites, evidence, measurement, speech-language/AAC, OT, behavioral support, mental health, accountability, technology and research preparation. Switch paths above My learning or Curriculum; common progress is retained.

sections.title: Distinct disciplines, coordinated questions
sections.text: Speech-language professionals, occupational therapists, behavioral professionals and mental-health clinicians have different training and scopes. A meaningful activity may involve several of them, but every child does not need every service. Caregivers contribute indispensable knowledge of everyday life. Professionals must practise within their competence and local requirements.

sections.title: What practical work means here
sections.text:
Cases are invented. Exercises use adult role-play, observation-language rewrites, activity analysis, literature appraisal and fictional plans. They do not ask you to diagnose a child, trial a treatment, administer a restricted test or upload a recording.

For a real concern, consult the appropriate qualified/local services. New loss of skills, health or hearing concerns deserve timely advice; immediate danger requires urgent local help. The studio does not assess individual symptoms.

sections.title: Age and source scope matter
sections.text: The curriculum spans ages 0–18, but individual resources do not all cover that range. ASHA’s public milestones cover birth–5. WHO Caregiver Skills Training primarily concerns ages 2–9 and is not an adolescent programme. NHS videos describe their own services. Topic notes identify these boundaries.

sections.title: AI is a tool to scrutinise
sections.text: The professional technology topic examines evidence, accessibility, authorship and child-data risks. A fluent generated explanation is not a diagnosis or treatment plan. This studio and Voice AI Studio are separate; nothing here authorises using a voice agent as a child’s therapist.

method.title: How to learn here
method.lead: Build an explanation you can defend, then practise, assess and revisit it.

sections.title: The learning loop
sections.text: Read the native explanation and prerequisite bridge. Work through the supplied example before revealing its explanation. Follow the exact readings/videos in order. Complete the practical task, attempt the independent assessment without the solution, and record evidence in your own words. Teach the idea to a partner and invite a challenge.

sections.title: Use the complete learning loop
sections.text: Read the guided explanation and its bridge first. In Watch & read, follow the topic-specific study assignment: it names the relevant sections and explains what each video covers. Complete the native worked exercise, compare your method with the solution, then attempt the independent task before opening its expected reasoning. Check every topic-specific criterion before recording a pass. A quiz answer or a short video alone is not a completed topic. Advanced source courses can take weeks; split a topic across sessions when needed.

sections.title: Prerequisites and honest passes
sections.text: You may explore any lesson. A recorded pass requires prerequisite passes, practice confirmation, a correct retrieval answer in the current session, confirmation of the criteria and at least 40 characters of assessment evidence. The website records your judgement; it does not automatically grade external work or establish competence.

sections.title: Recall after a delay
sections.text: After a pass, review after two days, then seven days after that review, then thirty days after the next. Recall first, check the source and try a changed example. If a foundation remains unclear, follow its prerequisite links rather than treating a progress percentage as proof of understanding.

sections.title: Depth and limits
sections.text: The professional path introduces advanced reasoning and authoritative guidance, but does not replace full scientific coursework, restricted assessment training, supervised clinical placements or regulation. Its capstone produces fictional case reasoning and a research proposal, not a clinical treatment plan.

sections.title: How long the route takes
sections.text: The caregiver route has 24 topics and the professional route 28, with 12 shared. At one fully completed topic per day, those are 24 or 28 study days; completing both unique paths means 40 topics. A topic includes sources, practice and assessment, so many need several sessions. Review days and formal professional training are additional.

sections.title: Sources and missing public videos
sections.text:
Sources include Harvard’s Center on the Developing Child, ASHA, WHO, NHS therapy services, Vanderbilt IRIS, NICE, NIMH, UNICEF, RCOT and AOTA. Provider scope and age ranges are listed per topic. The hub’s explanations and fictional cases are original study guidance, with no institutional endorsement.

The inventory was researched on 30 October 2026. Providers control captions, accounts, fees, availability and embedding. A linked source is not mirrored here or endorsed by its institution. Where a matched public video has not been verified, that gap is displayed and the lesson/readings remain available.

sections.title: Your account and privacy
sections.text:
Use your existing site learning account or create your own through the account panel. Each studio has separate progress storage, local cache, backup format and auth session. Guest work stays separate when you sign in; export then deliberately import if you want to move it.

Never enter a child’s identifiers, voice, photographs, diagnosis, assessment report or other clinical information. Use invented cases only. Clinical records belong in authorised professional systems. The account stores the adult learner’s educational progress, not child care records.

Use your own browser profile on shared devices. Export backups regularly. Clearing browser data removes unsynced work. Videos connect to YouTube only when loaded; provider links open externally.

sections.title: What completion means
sections.text: A self-assessed learning record describes the work you performed. It is not an accredited qualification, institutional exam credit or independent professional certification. The Qualifications page explains formal routes and their different requirements.

qualifications.title: Qualifications, learning records and professional routes
qualifications.lead: Decide whether your goal is caregiver education, a professional career or graduate research. These require different evidence and formal steps.

sections.title: What this studio awards
sections.text: The hub records self-assessed study progress, notes and portfolio evidence. It awards no accredited qualification, professional registration, clinical competence certificate or right to practise. Passing a topic means you judged your educational evidence against its criteria.

sections.title: Caregiver education and external learning records
sections.text: No clinical credential is required to understand development, ask informed questions or collaborate with a care team. Some external educational providers issue their own completion records. IRIS offers module-only access and, for eligible modules, a free account-based PD certificate route with pre/post assessments. This is professional-development documentation, not a therapy licence.

sections.title: Speech-language professional route
sections.text: Investigate an accredited qualifying programme, required supervised clinical education, examinations and registration in the country where you intend to practise. ASHA’s CCC-SLP is a specific US certification system with graduate education, supervised clinical requirements, examination and fellowship standards; it is not a worldwide licence. Verify current effective standards, application costs and local licensing separately.

links.label: ASHA — SLP certification standards and implementation

sections.title: Occupational therapy route
sections.text: A qualifying education and supervised practical training precede relevant professional registration/certification. In the UK, check HCPC approved programmes and registration requirements. In the US, NBCOT has its own education, eligibility, examination and international-review routes; state licensing is separate. Confirm your intended jurisdiction before enrolling or paying.

sections.title: Behavioral and mental-health routes
sections.text: Behavioral support is not one universal credential, and a behavior-analysis credential does not grant every mental-health therapy scope. BACB’s BCBA route has degree/coursework, supervised experience, examination, ethics and location/eligibility rules. Check the current handbook and country restrictions before planning it. Psychology, counselling and other mental-health professions have their own qualifying and regulatory routes.

links.label: BACB — BCBA eligibility and current handbook

sections.title: A practical next-step checklist
sections.text: Choose the profession and country first. Verify protected titles and regulator, approved programmes, scientific prerequisites, placement/supervision, assessed competencies, examinations, international recognition and total costs. Ask the programme/regulator directly where anything is unclear. Build a further-study plan from P16; do not represent this hub as a qualifying programme.

sections.title: Details checked 30 October 2026
sections.text: External rules, programme status, fees, eligibility and delivery can change. Follow the issuer’s current official requirements. No provider listed here endorses the studio or gives automatic credit for its progress.
